papers.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
papers.problem: Screen agents miss small buttons in cluttered screenshots and click the wrong control.
papers.fix: A small helper model crops and zooms the target area and adds a red circle plus a text hint.
papers.practicalUseCase: Frozen click models gain accuracy across five benchmarks without retraining, so add a zoom step before your agent clicks.
papers.limitation: The reported gains are average results on benchmarks, so your own screens may behave differently.

papers.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
papers.problem: Computer agents pass fixed benchmark tasks, but real users leave out details and add their own limits.
papers.fix: When 44 personas phrased the same 74 tasks, mean task completion fell by 36% across nine models.
papers.practicalUseCase: A high benchmark score overstates real use, so test your agent with vague, personal requests.
papers.limitation: The personas are simulated by another AI, not real people.

papers.title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
papers.problem: Trading simulators built from AI models may misprice how an agent's own orders move the market.
papers.fix: Five AI market models showed price impact on their own, with exponents from 0.63 to 1.21.
papers.practicalUseCase: Simulated impact runs above the usual 0.5 rule, so test a simulator against real markets before training agents.
papers.limitation: The models showed no impact decay after trades, which the authors link to short context windows.

papers.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
papers.problem: Image generators must learn both what things are and how to render fine pixel detail.
papers.fix: Learning meaning first with autoregression, then rendering with diffusion, trained a 3B model in 6,600 H100 GPU-hours.
papers.practicalUseCase: Strong image models can cost far less compute, so split meaning from rendering when you train your own.
papers.limitation: The scores come from two benchmarks, GenEval at 86 and DPG-Bench at 87, on one model size.

papers.title: Instruction Capacity: Behavior and Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load
papers.problem: Nobody could state how many instructions a language model can follow before quality drops.
papers.fix: GPT-4o mini held about 37 to 38 rules at 0.95 correct, and about 18 to 19 at full density.
papers.practicalUseCase: Long prompts with many rules fail quietly, so keep your prompt rules well under that limit.
papers.limitation: The test used word-swap rules on one model, so real tasks and other models may differ.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little was known about how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what drives issue size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, stronger security and longer debt terms gave larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger green or social sukuk should use equity-based contracts and strong security.
papers.limitation: The data shows links between factors and size, not cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority nations still lack formal financial services despite Islamic finance growth.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, education, institutions and internet access drive inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries should invest in digital infrastructure and in youth and women, because those levers raise inclusion.
papers.limitation: The panel regression shows links across countries, not proof of cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear what drives bank growth in countries with both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drove bank expansion most, and high-tech exports helped only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks and regulators should invest in digital systems first, because they pay off most for growth.
papers.limitation: The data covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other markets may differ.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether AI and big data help them compete.
papers.fix: Survey answers from 214 managers link AI, big data analytics and data management to higher competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic bank leaders should invest in AI and data practices, since managers tie them to better results.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian banks at one time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but their real effect on environmental work was unclear.
papers.fix: Committees raised environmental scores, products, innovation and resource cuts, yet in Islamic banks they mainly lifted overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: Regulators should not assume a committee changes Islamic bank products, so check what the bank actually launches.
papers.limitation: The study covers emerging markets only and shows links through panel regression, not cause.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students feel pressure to innovate, and it was unclear what helps them do it with generative AI.
papers.fix: Both inner drive and outside rewards raise innovation, and AI literacy strengthens how much motivation turns into new ideas.
papers.practicalUseCase: Build AI skills and good research support, because they help even when your motivation is low.
papers.limitation: Self-reported survey data from one point in time cannot prove which factor causes the other.

papers.title: Positive mood enhances accessibility of unrelated concepts in the first language but not in the foreign language
papers.problem: Bilingual people switch languages daily, but how mood changes their thinking in each language was unclear.
papers.fix: Positive mood widened word links in the first language, but left the foreign language unchanged.
papers.practicalUseCase: Mood may change how you think in your first language, so make big decisions in a steady mood.
papers.limitation: Brain recordings show this pattern in a lab setting, so everyday work may differ.
